Well, here is the logic behind why the sprint mechanic was detrimental in the fourth installment. Due to the increased movement speed, players have to pace their shots for greater distances in order to take out a sprinting target, so in this version, the maps all had large pacing to match the new movement speed. This means it created large open spaces, exaggerated sightlines, and made movement options fairly linear (meaning that due to the map scaling increase, the movement options you have are too far away, therefore you are far more predictable to an opponent, which naturally decreases the dynamics of gameplay). Also, due to this, we get cat-and-mouse-like gameplay of players preferring to run away and be chased down, which is very similar to a certain popular shooter style, rather than sticking in the fight or finding an interesting route to flank the opponent.

The souls series has always represented an existential crisis in my eyes. (Letting the fire extinguish and ushering in an age of darkness or continuing to nurture it). More specifically, existentialists argue that there is no inherent purpose to life other than what we choose to make it. I believe the essence of that idea is more about the player pursuing their desires and that the quest for "true purpose" is something people have been engaged in for so long when perhaps we shouldn't be. I think that the message here is more aligned with Carpe Diem (live life to the fullest). PS.... I am not an expert on the lore of this series, so I'm sure there are mistakes or inaccuracies in my understanding.
